differences.what: B's wordmark is crisp, legible white EARF type on the smoked acrylic. A's wordmark is half lost under a dark reflection streak and smeared by soft resampling.
A's whole frame looks over-sharpened and AI-upscaled: haloed edges and smeared detail on the plinth, feet and screws. B has natural grain and clean edges.
A's open dust cover takes up the top half of the frame. It is a large grey smoked slab with no clean highlights and it pulls the eye away from the deck.
A's record label is blank cream with no print and its spindle is barely there. B's label carries type and its spindle is metallic.
B's tonearm, counterweight and arm base read as believable polished metal with real highlights. A's arm is a flat black block with no material read.

A has a flat, shadowless white sweep and the product floats. B has a grounded contact shadow and a directional falloff that gives it depth, though B's black upper vignette is heavy and cuts the corner abruptly.
B's stacked acrylic plinth edges show confusing internal reflections and doubled lines along the front edge.
